confidence_rationale: Directly relevant to SD-031's 'single-pass' qualifier, which is the part of the claim most exposed to disconfirmation. Using a bias-free two-alternative forced-choice control-detection task with staircased difficulty (accuracy held at 70%) and signal-detection measures (d', meta-d') across 40 participants, the authors identify TWO distinct processes underlying first-order detection of control: one based on instantaneous sensory predictions for the current movement, and one based on detection of a regular motor-visual relation ACROSS A SERIES of movements. The first is a single-pass comparator of essentially SD-031's form; the second is a temporally-extended regularity detector that a single-pass residual cannot implement. Methodologically strong (bias-free d', staircase control, SEM, n=40, Haggard lab). Confidence 0.66 rather than higher because the paradigm again uses visuomotor object control rather than general world-state consequences, and because the dual-process decomposition is inferred from an individual-differences/SEM analysis rather than from direct manipulation of each process.
failure_signatures: First-order detection of control decomposes into at least two processes -- an instantaneous per-movement sensory prediction and a cross-trial motor-visual regularity detector -- so a purely instantaneous comparator captures only part of the attribution signal.

Metacognitive sensitivity was NEGATIVELY correlated with the predictive-process component, contradicting the hypothesis that detection of control relies on metacognitive monitoring of a predictive circuit and suggesting the predictive comparator operates unconsciously.

Large individual differences in metacognitive sensitivity persisted even when first-order sensitivity was experimentally equated, so aggregate agency measures can mask heterogeneous underlying mechanisms.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Two distinct processes underlie first-order detection of control: one based on instantaneous sensory predictions for the current movement, and one based on detection of a regular motor-visual relation across a series of movements. Metacognitive sensitivity was negatively correlated with the predictive-process component, inconsistent with the hypothesis that control detection relies on metacognitive monitoring of a predictive circuit, and suggesting predictive agency mechanisms operate unconsciously.
mapping.ree_translation: SD-031 specifies a SINGLE-PASS comparator: residual_world = z_world_observed - E2_world(z_world_{t-1}, a_actual), a per-timestep instantaneous prediction error. Wen et al. find that this instantaneous form is real and operative -- supporting SD-031's chosen mechanism -- but that it is only one of two contributors, the other being cross-trial regularity detection over a series of actions. For REE this is a scope finding rather than a refutation: SD-031's single-pass residual plausibly captures the first process well and the second not at all. The unconscious-operation result is separately reassuring, in that it removes any implicit requirement for a metacognitive or reportability layer above the comparator -- consistent with REE implementing attribution as a low-level signal.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Three boundaries. (1) The temporally-extended process may already be covered elsewhere in REE's architecture -- ResidueField-style causal tracking, which SD-031's own functional_restatement names as a downstream consumer, is a candidate -- so 'SD-031 does not implement it' is not automatically an architectural gap; this needs checking against the substrate before it is treated as one. (2) PARADIGM SCOPE: as with Ohata et al., the controlled consequence is visuomotor object motion, not the general non-harm world-state consequences z_world targets. (3) INFERENTIAL FORM: the two processes are separated by individual-differences and structural equation modelling, not by direct experimental manipulation of each, so the decomposition is correlational and the two components may be less cleanly separable than the analysis implies.
mapping.source_context: Human behavioural psychophysics; 40 healthy adults; two-alternative forced-choice control-detection task with staircase holding accuracy at 70%; signal-detection d' and meta-d'; structural equation modelling.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high: bias-free signal-detection measures, staircase-controlled first-order difficulty, n=40, established lab, and a result that runs AGAINST the authors' own prior hypothesis (which raises credibility). Mapping fidelity moderate: it speaks precisely to the single-pass qualifier but via a visuomotor paradigm, and the dual-process split is correlational rather than manipulated. Transfer risk moderate. Logged mixed because it simultaneously supports the reality of the instantaneous comparator and bounds its sufficiency.
